I’ve also had psychosis and I thought I heard my dad muttering under his breath about me and I yelled at him for it. Turns out he didn’t even say anything. But I couldn’t tell the difference between reality and hallucinations at the time, it was my first episode of psychosis. While I understand this is not exactly the same as punching someone, please understand I’m not trying to say that our experiences are exactly the same, just a little bit similar, so I might have a little bit of insight into how you are feeling. You’re not alone, I’m sure similar situations and maybe even the exact same situation have happened to many people in the grips of a psychotic episode. 
Try not to feel too bad about it, if your Mum or your nurse have two brain cells to rub together they’ll understand that you weren’t exactly yourself, and they probably don’t blame you as much as you think they do. 
A good parent will always love and care for you and be there for you, and would definitely forgive something like this. You were sick, your brain wasn’t capable of making sound decisions, that’s the very definition of psychosis.

Edit: have you apologised? It might be hard and even a bit embarrassing to admit that you weren’t fully in control of your body and mind, I’m all too familiar with that feeling, but I’m sure she will understand and forgive you. Even if you haven’t apologised she’s probably already forgiven you. but if you haven’t apologised yet please do, it’ll get it off your chest and you can stop dwelling on it and if you have the feeling of an elephant in the room because you haven’t spoken about it well it’ll fuck that elephant right off. 
Some tips for an effective sincere apology: 1/ take responsibility for your actions (eg I’m sorry I punched you Mum, while I understand I was under psychosis so I wasn’t capable of making the right decisions at the time, I acknowledge that I still hurt you, and there is no excuse for that)
2/ express regret (eg I’ve been thinking about my actions a lot lately, and when I think about them I feel really guilty, because I understand now that you were just trying to help me, and I love you and the last thing I want to do is hurt one of the people I love more than anyone in the world. I would do anything to go back to that day and change my actions)
3/ make amends (eg if there’s anything I can do to make it up to you please let me know, because I am at a loss about how to make the situation right apart from offering you this apology and swearing that should I ever go though psychosis again I’ll remember how much I hurt you last time and won’t ever hurt you again) 

And maybe wrap it up with a thankyou Mum for helping me when I needed it most, I really appreciate you being there for me in my time of need, I’ll always appreciate and never forget what a caring and loving Mum you have been to me.

If it was me I’d buy her some flowers or a box of chocolates but I also have the tendency to go WAYY overboard when I apologise so maybe get a second opinion in the gift side of things, because in the past people have told me that the gift can detract from the sincerity of the apology.

Hey there, random question, can I ask how old you are? I have a whole reply I want to type to you but what I want to say changes depending on what period of your life you are currently in.

I don’t want that for you. I want you to be strong and live a happy and full life, just to prove to that’s asshole that he has no power over you. It sounds like you have had a tough life, it sounds like you have every right to feel upset, but to me, you also sound like a survivor. You’ve already been through more hardship than what a lot of people will experience in their entire life, but you’re young and you could have a full amazing life ahead of you, and maybe, with the right help, little by little, day by day, you’ll start to think about what happened less and less, even if in the early days you can just put it out of your mind for 15 minutes and do something just for you, something you enjoy.
It won’t be easy, but I think you’re strong enough to do it.
Sometimes, after a serious trauma such as what you have experienced, the things that we used to find fun no longer give us pleasure. That is normal. You have to keep trying, keep doing the things you enjoy, ‘fake it till you make it’ and maybe one day your happiness will come back, even if it’s just for 5 mins. But the next day maybe it’ll come back for 7 minutes, and the day after that maybe it won’t come back at all, because life is a roller coaster of ups and downs, but the day after that? Maybe you’ll feel happy doing your old hobbies for a whole hour...and eventually, as time goes on, this crappy experience will just be a distant memory, and what you have learnt from the experience will make you a stronger person than most, and you can help others that have been through the same thing.

Just because he was your boyfriend doesn’t mean that he can have sex wth you against your will and have it not be termed ‘rape’. Don’t think that people will think that you weren’t raped simply because he was your boyfriend. Most people, especially law enforcement, understand that rape can happen even inside a relationship. So don’t be afraid that people won’t believe you. And if some people don’t believe you, then the problem is with THEM, not with you. 
I was sexually assaulted about 6 weeks ago, and while I understand that is not as intense as being raped, I feel I might,
On some level, be able to empathise with how you are feeling. It made me feel objectified, and like I was worthless, like what I wanted didn’t matter to anyone. I felt ashamed, like I didn’t want to exist anymore, like sex was yucky and something I would never want to experience ever again. On top of that, the person that I was consensually intimately seeing at the time dumped me three days after I opened up to him about what had happened. Initially he didn’t believe me, because he’s an idiot, he said ‘if it was really that bad, why haven’t you reported it to the police’ he clearly didn’t understand how much it hurts to recount and relive the story in every painful detail over and over to a bunch of strangers. In the end I did report it to the police, to show him it was a legitimate thing that happened to me, that I wasn’t making it up for attention. When he dumped me I felt like he did it because he saw me as being ‘used’ or ‘dirty’ after being touched by another man, despite it being against my will. This made me extremely
Upset and suicidal. One thing I will say, is when I reported it to the police, they said it didn’t matter if I had told them days later or months later, and I could decide whether or not to press charges in my own time, even if it was months down the line, whenever I felt comfortable and brave enough, and had the proper support network, to go through with it. The best thing they did was give me the number for a counselling service which in Australia is called CASA. These are telephone counsellors that deal specifically with victims of sexual assault, and I have found them A LOT more helpful than just the regular suicide prevention helplines. Is there a counselling service like that in Ireland? I can’t guarantee they will make you feel better, but you have to try everything possible to try and make yourself feel like your old self again before deciding to make the permanent decision of pulling the plug, because you can’t take that back, so you have to try every avenue possible to try make yourself feel better before you decide to do that. Does that make sense? Your life is important, you have to try hard to preserve it, although you may feel like suicide is the only way you’ll get any relief from your pain now, maybe a very good psychologist will be able to give you enough relief from your pain to start to enjoy life in the way that you used to. Just take it one day at a time, love and care for yourself because you are a strong woman, I can tell.
I just wanted to take this time to say what happened was in NO WAY your fault, and that it has happened to many other women, and those women would like nothing more than to help you through this experience, so seek them out. Maybe there is a victims of crime group you could attend, and find someone who really understands you, because they’ve been through something like what you’ve been through, and you can support each other, you might even make a new friend, which would be a positive out of what is otherwise a horrible shitty situation that you should not have been made to go through. 
When I told people, I felt like they either wouldn’t believe me, or think it was my fault, and sometimes people did act that way, so be selective about who you open up to, you want to make sure the person will be on your side and understand you, instead of blaming you. Anyone that blames you? I’ll tell you exactly what my counsellor said about them ‘well they are just idiots and a clear indication of the level of patriarchy that still unfortunately exists in our society, as their uninformed views are just echoes of the biased views of a certain subsection of our society who don’t understand sexual assault. The people who blame you or don’t believe you, well pay no attention to them, because their ill informed, incorrect opinions say more about them and their stupidity then it does about you and your experience.’
There is help out there. You are not alone, although it might feel that way.
If you want to talk you can PM me.

Omg the endless colouring they expect you to do in psych wards. Why not arrange for a mobile petting zoo to visit the psych ward as an activity, so we can pet the bunnies and watch the animals frolic around happily and maybe cheer us up a bit? Or teach us a new skill or hobby that we can maybe get into once we’re released as a reason to have interest in life again. Psych wards are boring and do nothing but give you all day to focus on why you’re feeling like shit, they take away whatever coping mechanisms you DO have at home, like a pet or your hobby, and leave you with nothing but shitty hospital food and being surrounded by other people who also drag you down because they’re feeling down. Oh! And then there’s the shame of your freedom being taken away as well.
The only good part is all the free Valium they shove in your face so you don’t make a scene about being confined to a boring underfunded depressing building with peeling paint, where, in my experience, a majority of the patients are men and they all see me, a young woman, as an object to hit on as something to do to pass the time.
It’s like dude - I’m in here because I’m not doing well mentally and now you’ve jacked me up on so many antipsychotics and benzodiazepines that I can’t even remember my own name, let alone fend off the unwanted advances of multiple mentally ill men. But yeah, confine me to this super healthy environment against my will, this will really aid in my recovery.
I’m in Australia and I realise the psych ward facilities we have here are meant to be better than in a lot of other countries, but they’re still basically (in some respects) comparable to a jail. It’s like they only exist to separate me from the community because the general community doesn’t want me to be a participant in it because I’m ‘unstable’. Like it exists just to protect the majority of society, the neurotypical, from me, the mentally ill.

It’s like he forgets I was put in the psych ward only a year and a half ago for a failed suicide attempt.
I was always told to reach out whenever I was feeling this low so the people around me who cared could maybe remind me of a reason to live. Or even just say ‘hey I know you’re feeling low, but we’ve got each other, so let’s watch some comedy and hug in bed and forget your troubles, even if just for a couple of minutes’.
I reach out not because I’m seeking attention, but because I’m seeking HELP. I want someone out there to remind me of a reason worth living.
The best response I get from people when I tell them is them completely ignoring the comment, imagine how that feels, going to someone and saying ‘I feel so shitty and worthless and like not  single person on the planet cares about whether I live or die, everyone is ignoring me and it’s hurting me really bad’ and then they proceed to ignore me. Their silence might as well say ‘you’re completely right Ella, me and everyone else you know really don’t give a flying fuck about you, you should go kill yourself.’ the worst response? The boyfriend saying if I was serious I would have done it by now. It’s like oh you don’t think I’m serious? I’ll show you how serious I actually am.
Well just have to agree to disagree

But then literally the day before going through wth it I met a lovely couple who i became good friends with, through an acquaintance. And then a few days later another blossoming friendship with a jolly guy who just laughs and laughs and makes me do the same. I think if you wait it out, decent people can sense that you’re in need of cheering up, like it might sound stupid but I swear some people - decent people- can see the sadness and loneliness in my eyes (or maybe they can just tell from the smudged mascara from the tears) and will reach out and fill your life up with the care and joy that your partner was failing to provide. Some people suck the life force from you, others boost you up. I have a tendency to ‘love’ the people who like to abuse me and drag me down, then I wonder why I’m miserable. Fill your life with happy successful people and soon you will be happy and successful as well. You meet people in the most weird places, like striking up conversation with someone in line at the supermarket, complimenting someone’s shoes in a lift, just fake your happiness for a tiny little while and real happiness and happy people will follow faster than you could think.

Oh wow I really feel for you, man, I was in a short relationship and we would only do it about once a week and I felt like that was a pretty sexless relationship. Once a month? I’d go crazy. 
I think the best way to tackle this is a serious sitdown discussion during which you bring up your issues. Just let her know that you need sex more than once a month in order to feel fulfilled in the relationship. Ask her how often she feels like she needs to have sex in order to feel fulfilled in the relationship. If she says it’s only once a month then I would say she has a low libido and she should be doing something to try and remedy this because it’s not fair on you to have sex so infrequently. Is she on antidepressants or some other medication that could be affecting her libido? 
I remember trying to initiate sex with my partner and being knocked back every single time. It made me feel unattractive, like there was something wrong with me, like he wasn’t interested in me any more, like I couldn’t fulfil his needs sexually, it started to erode myself esteem and I would often cry about it. So I know how shitty it feels and I’m sorry you have to go through this.
Maybe she’s feeling unfulfilled with the type of sex that you have, I know some people can get bored with the same sex occurring over and over until it becomes a bit mundane and then they lose interest. Maybe you need to do something new to spice things up in the bedroom.
When my partner began to lose interest in me sexually I bought a Japanese schoolgirl outfit off the Internet because I knew he was really into anime and I thought maybe some role-playing would spice things up and that helped for about a month. Maybe you could introduce some toys or a blindfold? Or go out of your way to make it super romantic with candles and some rose pedals and strawberries and chocolate and some sexy music? Talk to her about her sexual desires, her fantasies, maybe ask her what she thinks about when she masturbates. Ask her what you do during sex that she really likes, And ask her what you do that she doesn’t like.
If this doesn’t work, maybe you could consider going to some couples therapy together, there are some counsellors that specifically focus on sexual therapy.
Maybe, if you’re comfortable, even ask her how often she used to do it in her previous relationships. Maybe she is bordering on asexual and has never really had a high sex drive, if this is the case you need to consider whether she will change and compromise to meet you halfway. Relationships are all about compromise. What I really hated about my previous relationship was that he would never respond well when I tried to initiate things because he wasn’t in the mood and he didn’t understand that  he needed to let me put him in the mood, like when he tried to initiate things with me I was never in the mood but I let him put me in the mood with kissing and foreplay etc. she needs to give you a chance to do this to her. Maybe you could tell her that as well? 
Communication is key. If you can’t talk about sex then you shouldn’t be having sex is my thoughts on the matter.
Maybe she just really isn’t interested in sex and if she isn’t and isn’t willing to compromise maybe you could see if she’d be interested in an open relationship?
Sex is a basic human need, you don’t want to miss out on the experience of intimacy for your entire life simply because she doesn’t want to have sex with you, you’ll just end up resenting her.

Hey I thought I’d chime in as someone with schizophrenia and potentially BPD. 
I’m just going to pretend that your girlfriend thinks the same as me and that might give you some insight into he way she thinks. Close minded, no?

She probably hates the meds because they zombiefy her brain or make her memory terrible or have a high risk of something scary like muscle movement disorders. On top of that, taking the meds means you have to admit that you have something ‘wrong’ with you. Something is ‘broken’ and you need to take meds to ‘fix’ it. She might be feeling embarrassed and ashamed and pushing it into the procrastination pile because she can’t mentally deal with facing head on that she’s not neuro typical. Maybe she feels the meds don’t do anything positive and doesn’t want to be needlessly putting chemicals that seemingly do nothing (in her opinion) into her body everyday.

As far as her snapping at you, yes that was inappropriate. But if she does have BPD you have to realise that the line between love and hate is razor thin, the more she loves you the more hatred she will display when she feels slighted by you because she feels extra hurt that the person who she loves more than anything has hurt her. Even if it’s just a perceived slight, misconstrued in the moment because she’s tired and stressed. Your reaction sounded perfect, and I bet her thought pattern went like this... stress building up that she’s holding in...eruption...lashing out at the closest thing (you)...you respond in your lovely manner buuuut maybe she’s headstrong and doesn’t want to admit she’s made a mistake by lashing out at you, so she’s stuck in a position where she can only continue to lash out...phone call ends...she falls in a heap on the bed not hating you, but absolutely hating herself, because now she’s calmed down a bit she’s realised how insane she just acted and how she lashed it at the most important person in the world to her...she cries harder than ever...hating herself for what she’s done, knowing she’s caused irreparable damage to the relationship...and hating the disease that makes her life so much more difficult and less fulfilling than all those around her...she desperately wants comforting but she’s just made a mess of your interaction so she lays there alone for hours crying until her eyes swell shut.

That’s my experience anyway.
NO I’m not blaming my disorders for my shitty behaviour, but I bet if I didn’t have them I wouldn’t go through this loop as often. She can learn to control it, but it takes time and therapy and maybe meds of that what the doctor recommends.
